Legally (if he decides to sue) That could work only if he truly quit. He can sue . It is a Unilateral contract. The agreement was valid. But he haven't fulfilled his part of the Contract which is actually and factually quitting. He did at another store not his place of work. So he has suffered no harm neither has he consummated the consideration (quitting). Statement like "if you quit right now I will give you x amount of money..." Is a valid consideration for a legal agreement It doesn't matter if it was parol( spoken orally). It is still binding on the parties. In Unilateral contract, once the other party performs his side the contract is executed. The court will definitely pronounce that his money be paid. See Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.

Legally (if he decides to sue) That could work only if he truly quit. He can sue . It is a Unilateral contract. The agreement was valid. But he haven't fulfilled his part of the Contract which is actually and factually quitting. He did at another store not his place of work. So he has suffered no harm neither has he consummated the consideration (quitting). Statement like "if you quit right now I will give you x amount of money..." Is a valid consideration for a legal agreement It doesn't matter if it was parol( spoken orally). It is still binding on the parties. In Unilateral contract, once the other party performs his side the contract is executed. The court will definitely pronounce that his money be paid. See Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.
